 Common Judgment

These petitions were filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ each for the injuries sustained by them in the road traffic accident caused on 03.07.2019.
 02.
Hence these petitions were clubbed together for the purpose of recording common evidence.

The main petition is M.V.C.No.4722/2019 and it is clubbed with M.V.C.No.4723/19.
 03.
The brief facts in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 is as under:

It is submitted that on 03.07.2019 at about 03.00 p.m when the petitioner was riding the Motor Cycle bearing No.AP09AP8960 along with one Raju @ Rajendra Bohara as pillion rider on Muthanallur In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
2 Circle, Huskur Road, in front of Nambiyar Layout,
Kaggalipura (V), Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, one School Bus bearing No.KA01AC4794 came in rash  (SCCH3) 4 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to this impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Best hospital,
Chandapura and admitted as inpatient.
The petitioner had spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.

The petitioner prior to the accident was hale and healthy and was working as Security Guard and earning Rs.25,000/
per month.
Due to the accident till today he cannot attend his work and sustained disability and lost his earning capacity.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the offending school bus driver only.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said school bus.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence this petition.
04. The brief facts in M.V.C.No.4723/2019 is as under:

It is submitted that on 03.07.2019 at about 03.00 p.m when the petitioner was proceeding as pillion order in the Motor Cycle bearing No.
AP09AP8960 ridden by one Janak @ Bahadur Janak on Muthanallur Circle, Huskur Road, in front of Nambiyar Layout, Kaggalipura (V), Sarjapura Hobli,
 (SCCH3) 5 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 Anekal Taluk, one School Bus bearing No.
KA01AC4794 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to this impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Best hospital, Chandapura and admitted as inpatient.
The petitioner had spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
The petitioner prior to the accident was hale and healthy and was working as Security Guard and earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
Due to the accident till today he cannot attend his work and sustained disability and lost his earning capacity.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the offending school bus driver only.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said school bus.
Hence both In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
3 respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence this petition.
05. After service of notice, the respondents have appeared through their counsel and filed written statement in both petitions.

06. The averments of the written statement of the respondent No.1 in both petitions are as under :
 (SCCH3) 6 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19
It was the rider of the two wheeler who was rash and negligent riding the motorcycle has lead to the incident.
Thus the petitioners cannot claim against this respondent.
A complaint was lodged in this regard by the driver of the school bus.
The school bus was insured with the respondent No.2 which is valid from 24.05.2019 to 23.05.2020.
The said policy was in force at the time of alleged accident.
The school bus driver was holding valid driving licence.
The petitioners have filed this false petitions to claim unlawfully.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and prays to dismiss both petitions with costs.
07. The averments of the written statement of the respondent No.2 in both petitions are as under :
The petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties.
The rider of the motorcycle was not wearing helmet on the date of accident and does not hold valid driving licence.
The school bus driver was not at all responsible for the accident as he was proceeding slowly.
Hence this respondent is not an necessary party to this petition.

The petitioner/rider of the motorcycle under the influence of alcohol was riding the uninsured motorcycle in high speed and and in the process of overtaking ongoing vehicles came in right  (SCCH3) 7 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 side of the road, due to which he had lost control and dashed against the school bus which leads to the accident.
The school bus driver had lodged complaint to the police and the concerned police have registered the case in Cr.No.227/2019 and sent the blood samples to the laboratory.
Even the said police have filed chargesheet against the rider of the motorcycle for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 338 of IPC and U/s 181, 185, 196 of IMV Act.
That one Ganesh who was the complainant was not at all the eye witness and afterthought filed false counter complaint after nearly 17 days delay.
Even based upon this complaint a case was registered in Cr.No.250/19 In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
4 against the school bus driver.
Later the said I.O had filed B final report stating that the complaint lodged by one Ganesh is false.
However these petitions were filed only to make unlawful gain by taking advantage of having insurance.
Hence this respondent is not liable to indemnify the petitioners.
That the owner of the uninsured motorcycle had entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having driving licence.
However this respondent has issued policy in favour of the respondent No.1 which is valid from 24.05.2019 to 23.05.2020.
But liability is subject to proving of the case and terms and conditions of the policy.
The  (SCCH3) 8 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 school bus was not involved in the accident.
The accident took place due to the negligence of rider of the motorcycle/petitioner.
The school bus driver was not holding valid driving licence on the date of accident.
It is denied that due to the accident the petitioners have sustained disability and lost income as stated in the petitions.
This respondent has denied the manner of accident, injuries and income as stated by the petitioners.
The claim of the petitioners are excessive and prays to dismiss all petitions with costs.

08. In order to prove the case, the petitioners in both petitions, Doctor, Public Relation Officer, were got examined themselves as PW.1 to 4 and got marked 27 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 27 and closed their side.
09. By way of rebuttal, the Deputy Manager of the respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked eleven documents as per Ex.R.1 to 11 and closed their side.
10. Heard both sides in both petitions.
11. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed:
(SCCH3) 9 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19  ISSUES IN M.V.C.No.4722/2019
01. Whether the petitioner proves that he  has sustained grievous injuries in the accident In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs

5  occurred on 03.07.2019 at about 03.00 p.m,
 on Muthanallur Circle, Huskur Road, in front  of Nambiyar Layout, Kaggalipura Village,
 Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, due  to negligent act of driver of School Bus  bearing reg. No.KA01AC4794 as alleged in  the petition ?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?
If so, from whom at what  quantum ?
03 . What order or award?
ISSUES IN M.V.C.No.4723/2019  01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he  has sustained grievous injuries in the accident  occurred on 03.07.2019 at about 03.00 p.m,
 on Muthanallur Circle, Huskur Road, in front  of Nambiyar Layout, Kaggalipura Village,
 Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, due  to negligent act of driver of School Bus  bearing reg. No.KA01AC4794 as alleged in  the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?
If so, from whom at what  quantum ?

12. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:
 ISSUES IN M.V.C.No.4722/2019  Issue No.1 : In negative  Issue No.2 : In negative  Issue No.3 :

As per final order  for the following:
 ISSUES IN M.V.C.No.4723/2019

Issue No.1 : In negative  Issue No.2 : In negative  Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
6  13.
Issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 and issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.4723/2019
: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration as they are inter related with each other and common in order to avoid repetition of facts.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that they have sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of School Bus driver bearing No.
KA01AC4794.
Due to the accident they have  (SCCH3) 11 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 sustained disability and lost income.

The same was opposed by the respondents and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of school bus driver and it is due to the negligence of rider of the motorcycle/petitioner.
The insured vehicle is falsely implicated in this case in order to claim compensation.

Hence they are not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
 14.
To prove this, the petitioner of M.V.C.No.4723/19 was got examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "The two wheeler in which I was proceeding was rode by my friend Bhadur Janak.
We were residing in same room.
The said vehicle belongs to our owner where we work.
I was not wearing helmet on that day, the rider was wearing helmet.
I saw the school bus it came in hight speed and dashed against our vehicle.
The place of accident is a single road, but two vehicles can move at a time.
It was a schol bus and the student/children were present in the bus.
At that time one cement lorry ws proceeding ahead of our vehicle.
It is true that the right portion of the bus touched our vehicle.
The bus driver did not stop the vehicle after causing accident.
It is true that they took  (SCCH3) 12 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 our breathe smell sample.
Complaint is not given by me and neither by Bahadur Janak.
Police have not come to the hospital and not recorded my statement.
It is true that complaint ws lodged after 17 days by one Ganesh.
I am working as security guard, but I do not have any documents in this regard.
It is true that after the accident I went to Nepal.
I am doing agriculture.
Now I am not going for any work.
I am depending on others".
Apart from this the PW.1 had denied other suggestion of the respondents counsel.
In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
7  15.
Further another injured and the claimant in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 was got examined himself as PW.2 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
In his cross examination he has admitted that "Ganesh is our Field Officer.
He is not the eye witness for the accident.
It is true that on the date of accident Ganesh was knowing that we met with accident.
Police came after two weeks to the hospital.
I got to know that bus driver has given complaint before Ganesh gave complaint.
I am having driving licence.
I cannot produce the driving licence as I lost it.
I obtained it from Nepal Government.
It is true that it is not valid in India.
It is true that I was not wearing helmet at that time.
At the place of accident the road is so wider and two big vehicles cannot move at a time.
(SCCH3) 13 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19
It is true that a lorry was proceeding ahead of our vehicle.
I did not see the bus.
It is true that the chargesheet was filed against me.
It is true that I was chargesheeted for drunk and driving, not having licence and not having insurance.
I am not doing any work as my leg is amputed".
Apart from this the PW.2 had denied all suggestion of the respondents counsel.
16. Per contra, the Deputy Manager of the respondent No.2 has got examined himself as RW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the written statement in his affidavit.

In his cross examination the Rw.1 has admitted that "It is true that in the said complaint the school bus driver had stated that the rider and pillion rider of motorcycle sustained injuries and he himself took them to the hospital.
It is true that in none of the police records they have not stated that the rider and pillion rider were not wore helmet as they have left it.
We did not enquired about the blood report of the injured which were sent by the police.
It is true that as on the date of alleged accident the policy of school and driving licence of its driver are valid ".
The RW.1 had denied all other suggestion of the petitioners counsel.
17. The PW.1 and 2 in support of their case got marked entire police documents at Ex.P.1 to 5 and 8.

So on perusal of these documents, it is clear that the  (SCCH3) 14 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 concerned I.O after investigation has filed chargesheet against one of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle namely Janak Bahadur for the alleged offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of IPC and U/s 181, 185,
196 of IMV Act stating that the rider of motorcycle due In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
8 to his rash and negligent riding dashed to the school bus.
Due to this the rider of the motorcycle and bus driver were sustained injuries.
Further the said I.O have stated that the rider of the motorcycle had rode the motorcycle in speed manner without having driving licence, insurance and by consuming alcohol.
18. So as per the documents produced by the PW.1 and 2 it reveals that the accident took place due to the negligence of rider of motorcycle.
So they will be termed as tortfeasor and they have filed these petitions claiming compensation against the school bus and its insurer.

19. It is not disputed that soon after the accident the school bus driver had lodged complaint to the police and the petitioners have contended that out of influence the school bus driver had lodged false complaint against the petitioners and this reason assigned by the petitioners cannot be accepted.
It may be true that the petitioners are uneducated and not residents of this country.
But this does not mean that  (SCCH3) 15 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 they should disobey the law where they resided.
According the law of this country the mistake of fact can be excused but the mistake of law cannot be excused.
Every person of this country ought to know the law of land.
Further it is not the case that the petitioners were unaware about lodging of complaint to the police.
Even the complainant namely Ganesh who is the field officer who had lodged complaint on behalf of the petitioners after 17 days of the alleged accident.
Even no valid reason is assigned for lodging the complaint after 17 days of the accident which throws doubt.
It is admitted by the PW.1 and 2 that the said Ganesh had lodged complaint after they came to know about lodging of complaint by the school bus driver.
So the respondents have rightly contended that the complaint lodged by said Ganesh is only an afterthought.

20. Further the RW.1 in support of their version had got marked 11 documents as Ex.R.1 to 11 i.e true copy of policy, invoice, notice issued to the R.C owner,
copy of FIR and complaint in both Cr.No.227/19 and Cr.No.250/19, 'B' final report and chargesheet.
It is also admitted that the concerned I.O after receiving complaint from both school bus driver and one Ganesh have taken up investigation.
It is also true that the  (SCCH3) 16 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
9 police have filed 'B' final report stating the complaint filed by one Ganesh against the school driver is false and they have filed chargesheet against the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle based upon the complaint lodged by the school bus driver.
 21.
The petitioners unlike in civil cases have to prove the fraud or influence in filing chargesheet against the rider of motorcycle/petitioner.
But in the instant case apart from making allegation there are no other supportive documents to prove that the false chargesheet was filed against the rider of motorcycle/petitioner.
It is true that the petitioners have challenged the chargesheet filed against the rider of motorcycle/petitioner before Anekal court which is still pending.

22. The petitioners have contended that out of influence a false case is registered against the rider of motorcycle/petitioner, but they have not proved it as there is no supportive oral and documentary evidence.
Even the petitioners have not cared to examine the I.O who had filed 'B' final report against the complaint lodged by one Ganesh.
Simply challenging the B final report itself will not prove that the school bus driver had caused the alleged accident.
(SCCH3) 17 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19  23. Further the petitioners have contended that there is contributory negligence of both rider of motorcycle and school bus driver.
But in support of this contention the petitioners have not produced any supportive documents.
This contention is against the averments of the petitions.
The contributory negligence means failure of an injured to act prudently considered factor in the injury which they have suffered.
Hence with the available documents on record even the contributory negligence cannot be considered.
24. Further the petitioners have contended that due to composite negligence they are at liberty to claim compensation against any or one of the tortfeasors.
The composite negligence means the negligence on part of two or more persons.
Even if this principle is not applicable to the facts of this case.
With the available documents on record it is clear that the rider of the motorcycle/petitioner in order to overtake on going vehicle with high speed had rode the motorcycle and caused the accident.

25 . The counsel for petitioners have relied upon decisions reported in  a. (2015) 9 SCC 273 - Khenyei V/s New India Assurance Company Limited and others - It is  (SCCH3) 18 MVC.No.4722/19 In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs

entities.text: Khenyei V/s New India Assurance Company Limited and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
10  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 observed that in case of joint tortfeasors compensation can be awarded against sole tortfeasor.
b. (2002) 6 SCC 455 - Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri V/s Karmasey Kunvargi Tak and others -

entities.text: Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri V/s Karmasey Kunvargi Tak and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that contributory negligence means breach of any duty.
It only means the failure by a person to use reasonable care for the safety of either himself or his property.
26. The above preposition of law is not applicable in favour of the petitioners as they have not either the contributory or composite negligence for the accident.
It is true and clear that the accident was caused by the rider of motorcycle/petitioner.
27. Further the rider of the motorcycle/petitioner was not holding valid driving licence.
It is true that he hold the driving licence issued by Nepal Government which is not valid in this country.
Even the copy of the said driving licence issued by the Nepal Government in the name of the rider of the motorcycle was not produced before this court.
28. Even it is clear that the motorcycle ridden by the rider/petitioner was not duly insured as required under law.
Hence the rider of  (SCCH3) 19 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 motorcycle/petitioner has violated the traffic rules by riding the uninsured vehicle on public road.
29 . Further the respondents have contended that on the date of accident the rider of the motorcycle/ petitioner had consumed alcohol.
It is true that the concerned I.O have chargesheeted the rider of the motorcycle/petitioner for this offence also.
But the PW.2 has got marked the FSL report as Ex.P.9 which states that the ' color tests and gas chromatographic methods have not responded for the presence of alcohol in article No.1 to 4'.
So as per Ex.P.9 the PW.2 has proved that he has not consumed alcohol on the date of accident.

30 . Therefore under these circumstances the petitioners have utterly failed to prove that they have sustained injuries due to the negligent driving of the school bus driver and entitled for compensation.
However the respondents have disproved the allegation of the petitioners.
Merely the petitioners have sustained injuries and spent amount for their treatment is not a ground to grant compensation to them.
The rider of the motorcycle/petitioner being one In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
11
of the tortfeasor is not entitled for the compensation.
Further another injured/pillion rider had sustained injuries due to the negligent riding of the rider of the  (SCCH3) 20 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 motorcycle in which he was proceeding.
Hence when they have not established the negligence of the school bus driver for the accident then they are not entitled for the compensation as claimed from the respondents.

The petitioner/rider of motorcycle being the tortfeasor cannot claim compensation for his own negligence from the respondents Hence I answered the issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 in negative and issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.4723/2019 in negative.

31. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 and issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.4723/2019: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration as they are inter related with each other and common in order to avoid repetition of facts.
32 . Further the petitioners have stated that due to the accident they are not able to do work as earlier and sustained disability.
In this regard they have got examined the doctor and Public Relation Officer as PW.3 and 4.

But when the petitioners have not proved the negligence of the school bus driver for the accident then the documents marked at Ex.P.6, 7, 9 to 27 could not taken into consideration and the petitioners are not entitled to receive any compensation from the respondents.

Regarding liability : The respondent No.2 eventhough admitted issuance of the policy in the name of the respondent No.1, but the petitioners are not successful in proving that they have sustained injuries due to the negligence of the school bus driver.

It is true that the school bus is owned by the respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2 but they are not liable to indemnify the petitioners.
Hence I answered the issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.
4722/2019 in negative and issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.
4723/2019 in negative.
34. Issue No.3 in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 and issue No.3 in M.V.C.No.4723/2019
: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration as they are inter related with each other and common in order to avoid repetition of facts.
35. Further as per my above findings it is clear that the petitioners are not entitled for any In: Mr.Janak @ Bahadur Janak vs In: 01.

The Head Master on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85248642/
12 compensation payable by the respondents as they have not proved their case beyond all preponderance of probabilities and also not proved that they have sustained injuries due to the negligence of the school bus driver which was owned by the respondent No.1 and insured with the respondent No.2.

As such I proceed to pass the following :
 (SCCH3) 22 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19  ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is dismissed with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner in M.V.C.No.4723/2019 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is dismissed with costs.
The original Judgment shall be kept in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 and copy of the same shall be kept in M.V.C.No.4723/2019.
The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ each.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated directly to the Stenographer on computer, got typed by him, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 20th day of February 2023).

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to the accident they have  (SCCH3) 11 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 sustained disability and lost income.
The same was opposed by the respondents and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of school bus driver and it is due to the negligence of rider of the motorcycle/petitioner.
Hence they are not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
 14.
It may be true that the petitioners are uneducated and not residents of this country.
But this does not mean that  (SCCH3) 15 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 they should disobey the law where they resided.
According the law of this country the mistake of fact can be excused but the mistake of law cannot be excused.
Every person of this country ought to know the law of land.
Further it is not the case that the petitioners were unaware about lodging of complaint to the police.
Even the complainant namely Ganesh who is the field officer who had lodged complaint on behalf of the petitioners after 17 days of the alleged accident.
Even no valid reason is assigned for lodging the complaint after 17 days of the accident which throws doubt.
The petitioners unlike in civil cases have to prove the fraud or influence in filing chargesheet against the rider of motorcycle/petitioner.
But in the instant case apart from making allegation there are no other supportive documents to prove that the false chargesheet was filed against the rider of motorcycle/petitioner.
With the available documents on record it is clear that the rider of the motorcycle/petitioner in order to overtake on going vehicle with high speed had rode the motorcycle and caused the accident.
It is true and clear that the accident was caused by the rider of motorcycle/petitioner.
27. Further the rider of the motorcycle/petitioner was not holding valid driving licence.
It is true that he hold the driving licence issued by Nepal Government which is not valid in this country.
Even the copy of the said driving licence issued by the Nepal Government in the name of the rider of the motorcycle was not produced before this court.
Hence the rider of  (SCCH3) 19 MVC.No.4722/19  c/w MVC.No.4723/19 motorcycle/petitioner has violated the traffic rules by riding the uninsured vehicle on public road.
However the respondents have disproved the allegation of the petitioners.
Merely the petitioners have sustained injuries and spent amount for their treatment is not a ground to grant compensation to them.
Hence when they have not established the negligence of the school bus driver for the accident then they are not entitled for the compensation as claimed from the respondents.
The petitioner/rider of motorcycle being the tortfeasor cannot claim compensation for his own negligence from the respondents Hence I answered the issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.4722/2019 in negative and issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.4723/2019 in negative.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Simply challenging the B final report itself will not prove that the school bus driver had caused the alleged accident.
The contributory negligence means failure of an injured to act prudently considered factor in the injury which they have suffered.
Hence with the available documents on record even the contributory negligence cannot be considered.
The composite negligence means the negligence on part of two or more persons.
